The Architecture

A 1916 Neo-Georgian, taken down to the studs between 1999 and 2001 and brought back without losing the year it was made.

Built1916 · Neo-Georgian
Restored1999–2001 · Thomas O'Shea, Architect
Living Area6,320 sq ft · plus 707 sq ft climate-controlled basement
Grounds4.15 acres · gated entry · circular drive
BrickworkRare handmade red brick, laid in Flemish bond over a traditional water table. Matching the historic brick took three months of curation.
Original 1916 FabricSeven carved mantels, restored oak floors, leaded sidelights, arched fanlights above six-panel solid-wood doors, original brass key plates, the dining-room frontispiece, the arched shell cabinets.
The Principal Rooms
The Drawing RoomNearly forty feet, two sitting areas. Federal-style carved mantel, dark marble surround, coffered and paneled ceiling, arched built-in bookcases, French doors to the rear brick terrace.
Sitting RoomA Delft-tile fireplace and a spiral staircase rising to the second-floor study.
Formal Dining RoomFireplace, the original 1916 frontispiece, arched shell cabinets, period moldings.
LibraryFloor-to-ceiling built-in shelving.
KitchenReclaimed heart-pine floors, custom white Shaker cabinetry, glass-front display, black granite, a professional stainless range and hood, full-size refrigerator, custom pull-out pantry, kitchen desk. The breakfast room wears chinoiserie toile and opens to the grounds.
Butler's PantryFarm sink and butcher-block counter.
Second-Floor Study / DenFloor-to-ceiling built-ins, a fitted desk run, the spiral stair down to the sitting room.
EntryTwo stories, a Colonial Revival staircase, an oak handrail running unbroken from volute to landing.
Bedrooms & Baths

A first-floor primary that takes the full depth of the house, and three more above it — each with its own fireplace.

Primary Suite — Main LevelCeladon millwork, dentil cornice, a mantel built into the panels. Two dressing rooms with built-ins and walk-in closets. The bath: chandelier, marble counters, Jacuzzi tub, oversized stone-tile walk-in shower, French doors to the grounds.
Second FloorThree generously scaled bedrooms, each with a fireplace and full bath. Two of the three baths have Jacuzzi tubs; two bedrooms open to a balcony.
The Count4 bedrooms · 4 full baths · 2 powder rooms
Pool & Tennis
Saltwater Pool20 × 40 ft, in-ground concrete, ringed by a brick wall with iron gates. Converted from chlorine to saltwater in 2022; machinery serviced annually.
TennisTwo regulation courts within the grounds — commercial-grade fencing, lighting for night play.In the interest of plain dealing: the courts are due for resurfacing.
The Grounds & Terrace
Brick Terrace30 × 23 ft for entertaining and al fresco dining — reached from the dining room and through the drawing-room French doors.
BalconyAbove the kitchen, off two of the upstairs bedrooms, over the courts and rear grounds.
Side PorchSink with hot and cold water, built-in cabinets, gardening shelves.
ParkingA primary area off the entry circle for twelve-plus cars; a second by the pool for six.
Systems & Stewardship

The quiet work that keeps a hundred-year-old house easy to live in.

FireplacesSeven — six on propane gas logs, switched and timed.
StaircasesThree.
ClimateFive HVAC units. A 250-gallon buried propane tank.
WaterCounty water and sewer to the home. A 130-ft well with an 80-gallon tank supplies irrigation and pool. Three electric hot-water heaters.
IrrigationA 28-plus-zone system — front, sides, rear, and into the woods.
MonitoringA Moen smart water monitor — app-connected, leak detection, remote shutoff.
SecurityHard-wired, with smoke alarms, remotely monitored.
UtilitiesAll underground.
Basement707 sq ft, climate-controlled, stone-walled — four rooms beneath half the house, with a wine rack, cold storage, and an exterior door.

The house was not built for spectacle. It was built for coming back.
